column3: Repeats “God” as the subject of both seeing and separating, rather than using “He” the second time.
“Day one” preserves the cardinal number rather than “the first day.”
“Heavens” preserves the same Hebrew noun used elsewhere for the heavens, rather than “sky.”
Explicitly locates the vegetation “on the earth” and says that the tree’s seed is “in it.”
The stars occur as a further object of “made,” without a separate repeated “He made.”
“Before the face of the expanse” preserves the spatial image rendered “in the open expanse.”
“And let them rule” preserves the plural subject and a distinct governing verb, rather than the purpose phrase “to rule.”
Repeats “God” as the subject of blessing and speaking.
The food provision continues elliptically from the preceding verse, without a repeated explicit “I have given.”
